tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description:
Read a page, PDF or feed as markdown, or only the part that answers the question. Text starts with [meta] JSON, then evidence; cite [meta].url. ok:false, content_ok:false or thin:true is unresolved: follow next_action.
Cheapest view first:
1. Is X there? must_contain: per-term found ×count with sections and excerpts, or not found. unverified = part of the page was unread, so absence proves nothing.
2. Where is X? focus: matching passages only, best first, under their section path; a miss returns the outline.
3. Long page: toc (sN ids, sizes), then section="sN".
4. No view: the page. A cut-off response has next_offset: repeat the call with offset. next_page names a paginated article's next part.
Walls (login, paywall, bot) fail fast and say which. Sites with a structured source (GitHub, Reddit, Stack Overflow, Wikipedia, registries) come back from it.

url.description: http(s) URL or an S/L handle from earlier output; an array of up to 12 reads them in parallel, each with the same view, max_chars shared across them.

must_contain.description: Presence check instead of reading: a phrase (case, spacing, quote/dash style and markdown emphasis ignored), a /regex/ (flags imsx), or a list of up to 8. Returns per term: found ×count, sections (sN) and excerpts; or not found, with a near-miss hint. Verdict match|partial|no_match|unverified (part of the page unread: absence proves nothing). Searches the whole page, or only section. Not with focus, toc, offset or since_last.

focus.description: Question or keywords: returns only matching passages, best first, under their §sN section path, and names query words absent from the page. A miss returns the outline, never the whole page. With section, ranks inside that part.

toc.description: Return the heading outline: [sN] ids with sizes, no body. With section, that part's outline only.

section.description: One part: an sN id from toc, or heading text (exact first, else first containing it). Includes subsections; no match returns the outline.

offset.description: Continue a cut-off response: its next_offset, with the same url and view arguments.

max_chars.description: Most characters returned (default 16000, ~4 per token); longer results end with next_offset. For a url array it is the batch total (default 48000).

links.description: Keep links. true or "urls": [text](real URL), to cite, check or follow a link. "handles": [text](L-handle), about half the tokens; a handle passed as url follows it. Off: link text only (~30% fewer tokens).

since_last.description: Change check against your previous read of this url: an unchanged line, or only the changed sections; with no earlier read, the page itself. Not with view arguments.

image_text.description: OCR the first 4 content images into an 'image text' section that every view searches. Slower; only when the evidence is in an image.

deadline_ms.description: Hard time limit in ms (500-600000): a deadline error on expiry, never a hang. Per URL in a batch.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Discover ranked URLs, titles and snippets; fetch a candidate for its full text. A snippet supports only what it states. A sources census names who answered and what every other source said, so an incomplete set reads as incomplete. Fetch handles resolve directly in web_fetch; citation URLs accompany the evidence in the leading [meta] JSON.

query.description: Primary search formulation. Include required entities, dates, versions and exclusions; do not include a guessed answer.

query_variants.description: Optional array; maximum 2 alternate formulations for the same unmet requirement. Preserve entities and hard constraints; vary vocabulary, terminology, language or answer-bearing phrasing. Omit when no distinct retrieval angle exists.

lang.description: Optional BCP-47 language tag (en, uk, ne, pt-BR). It selects the answer language; a region subtag is the only way to select a market. Omit for the English default on Latin-script queries; no language or country is inferred from the query's script. An explicit lang uses the local language-aware sources; configured providers are bypassed for that call.

max_results.description: Maximum ranked candidates to return (default 7, max 12). Increase only when the returned candidate set is insufficient.

deadline_ms.description: Hard time budget in ms (500-600000) for the whole call; per-backend timeouts stay below it. On expiry: an honest deadline error.

read.description: Read the top N results (max 3, default 0) within the call's deadline: their snippets become the page's own passage for the query (`page:`), and a follow-up web_fetch of them is served warm. Use when snippets are not enough to choose.

intent.description: auto (default) detects from the query. Keyless mode adds first-party sources: code: + GitHub, HN, StackExchange, MDN, crates.io/npm/PyPI for a package name; paper: + OpenAlex, arXiv, Europe PMC (biomedical); news or a recent window ('this week'): + news wire, publisher feeds, HN; entity: + Wikipedia; web: general only. With a configured provider, intent selects that provider's filters instead (one provider; the keyless verticals do not join).

tools.name: web_crawl
tools.description: Read multiple pages of a known site within explicit budgets. Text starts with [meta] JSON containing completion, page URLs and resume state. FrontierEmpty is complete only if evidence was obtained without failed or excluded pages; budget, deadline, throttle, cancellation and depth stops are incomplete. Cite page URLs. dataset=true returns JSONL after the metadata line.

url.description: Seed http(s) URL to crawl from; omit when continuing with resume.

mode.description: full (default) discovers pages and reads content; map returns only the URL inventory (a site map when one exists, otherwise the seed page's links, with no page fetches); content follows links from the seed when no usable site map exists.

focus.description: Topic or question for selecting relevant pages and passages. Set when the request targets one subject; omit only when the whole site scope is relevant.

map_limit.description: Max URLs returned in the inventory (default 120, range 1-50000). A capped inventory is incomplete; narrow focus/include_paths for large sites.

max_depth.description: Max link depth from seed (default 2). 0 = seed only.

max_total_chars.description: Total extracted-char budget across all pages (default 60000, range 1-500000).

per_page_max.description: Max markdown chars per page (default 8000, range 1-40000).

include_paths.description: Path globs to include (e.g. ["/docs/*"]). Empty = all.

same_host.description: Stay on seed's host (default true). false = follow cross-domain links.

deadline_s.description: Hard crawl deadline in seconds (default 120, range 1-600). Partial results return after.

since_last.description: Re-fetch pages and return only new or changed source fingerprints. Prior crawls or fetches supply per-URL baselines. Saves output, not verification requests; use for repeated reads.

dataset.description: Dataset mode: return JSON Lines (one JSON object per page) instead of markdown.

resume.description: Opaque token returned by a stopped crawl. Send it instead of url to continue saved progress; do not invent or alter it. A new crawl requires url and omits resume.

tools.name: web_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a URL as a rendered PNG in the browser. Returns an image content block and [meta] JSON with path and bytes. The path is server-local; use the inline image on remote clients. Full-page captures can be several MB. Private/loopback URLs are blocked like fetch. Failures return ok:false, code and next_action.

full_page.description: Capture the full page height, not just the viewport.

wait_ms.description: Extra milliseconds to wait after load, max 5000.

deadline_ms.description: Hard time budget in ms (500-600000, default 60000). On expiry: an honest deadline error with next_action, never a silent hang.
